items.summary: An integer overflow when compiling a specially crafted regular expression lets an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on self-managed GitLab CE/EE, affecting all versions from 7.0 (2014) up to the fixed releases. There is no workaround: upgrade to 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6 or the other patched lines; GitLab.com is already fixed.

Missing authentication for a critical function in Microsoft Azure Kubernetes Configuration Service allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network, with no authentication or user interaction required.
Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') in VM Inspector for Azure Virtual Machines allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

SQL injection in on-premises Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator can let a remote attacker access privileged internal functionality. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 23 after confirmed active exploitation; fixes are in versions 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12.

A stack buffer overflow in Wasmtime lets a malicious WebAssembly guest write about 16KB to the native stack via unvalidated async callback result types, potentially crashing the host or escaping the sandbox. It affects Wasmtime 39.0.0 before 48.0.4 and 49.0.0 before 49.0.2; update to a fixed release.
